questions.question: A Grade 3 (third-degree) soft tissue injury is characterised by:

options.B: Near-complete or complete tear/avulsion of the tissue, often with instability if a ligament is involved, and stress to the tissue being usually painless

questions.explanation: A Grade 3 injury involves near-complete or complete tear/avulsion of the tissue (tendon or ligament); notably, stress to the injured tissue is usually painless (since it's fully torn), and a torn ligament results in joint instability — a key distinguishing feature from Grade 1 and 2 injuries.

questions.question: What key feature distinguishes an obsession from a delusion?

options.A: An obsession is recognised as irrational and ego-alien, and the patient tries to resist it; a delusion is firmly believed and not resisted
options.B: A delusion always involves washing rituals while an obsession never does
options.D: There is no meaningful difference between the two

questions.explanation: An obsession is recognised by the patient as their own thought, but perceived as foreign (ego-alien), irrational, and something they try (unsuccessfully) to resist — insight is present. A delusion, by contrast, is a fixed false belief that the patient does not recognise as irrational and does not resist, because they genuinely believe it.

questions.question: Why does ischaemia (reduced blood/oxygen supply) lead to cell swelling and damage?

options.A: Ischaemia has no effect on the Na+-K+ pump
options.B: Ischaemia decreases Na+-K+ pump activity, disrupting osmotic equilibrium and allowing the cell to swell
options.C: Ischaemia directly ruptures the cell membrane through mechanical force
options.D: Ischaemia only affects extracellular fluid, never intracellular volume

questions.explanation: The Na+-K+ pump normally keeps osmotic equilibrium by moving positive charge (and effectively solute) out of the cell, counteracting the tendency of intracellular protein anions and other molecules to draw water in and cause swelling. Ischaemia reduces the ATP-dependent pump's activity, disrupting this balance — which is why prolonged cerebral ischaemia, causing cell swelling and damage, is often fatal.
questions.sourceBook: AK Jain, Physiology
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The four-point crutch gait is the sequence:

options.C: Both crutches together then both feet
options.D: Right crutch, left foot, left crutch, right foot

questions.explanation: It is the slowest but most stable gait, used in bilateral weakness or poor balance.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Pulmonary rehabilitation in COPD includes:
questions.explanation: Typically 6–8 weeks of twice-weekly supervised sessions; improves dyspnoea and quality of life.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Vapocoolant (ethyl chloride) spray is used with stretch in:
questions.explanation: The spray provides a cold stimulus that inhibits pain while the muscle is stretched.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The unit of capacitance is the:
questions.explanation: Inductance is measured in henries; magnetic flux density in tesla.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The usual temperature range for a warm whirlpool for a limb is:
questions.explanation: Whole-body Hubbard tank water is kept near 35–37 °C.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: A ‘foot slap’ at initial contact indicates weakness of the:
questions.explanation: Eccentric control of plantar flexion is lost, so the foot drops quickly onto the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: A Kirschner wire (K-wire) is used for:

options.B: Fixing small bone fragments and as a temporary fixation

questions.explanation: Also used for skeletal traction.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: In the 'dual process theory' of clinical reasoning, 'Type 1' thinking is best described as:

options.B: Intuitive, fast, automatic, and pattern-recognition based, but more vulnerable to error
options.D: A thinking style with no relevance to medical practice

questions.explanation: Type 1 thinking is intuitive, heuristic, automatic, fast, and effortless — highly efficient (used in roughly 95% of daily decisions) but more vulnerable to error and more affected by context than Type 2 thinking, which is slow, deliberate, and analytical.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Clinical Decision Making — Type 1 and Type 2 Thinking
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: For chronic tendon lesions, which continuous ultrasound intensity is generally used?
questions.explanation: Acute lesions: pulsed low-intensity (0.1–0.5 W/cm²).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The number of degrees of freedom of a hinge joint such as the elbow (humeroulnar) is:
questions.explanation: Uniaxial joints have 1 degree of freedom; condyloid 2; ball-and-socket 3.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Under the Biomedical Waste Management Rules, human anatomical waste is disposed of in:
questions.explanation: Yellow: anatomical/soiled waste; red: contaminated recyclable plastics; white translucent: sharps; blue: glassware.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Electrical power in watts equals:
questions.explanation: P = VI = I²R = V²/R.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: In competitive inhibition, the inhibitor:

options.A: Increases the apparent Km without changing Vmax

questions.explanation: Competitive inhibition can be overcome by increasing substrate.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Physiotherapy for Bell's palsy emphasises:

options.C: Facial massage, gentle mirror exercises and eye protection; avoid vigorous electrical stimulation early

questions.explanation: Eye care prevents corneal ulceration.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Shumway-Cook & Woollacott, Motor Control; standard neurology texts (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Weakness of the rhomboids is demonstrated by:

options.B: Weak scapular adduction and downward rotation, with the scapula lying lateral to the spine

questions.explanation: Tested prone with the hand on the buttock lifting the scapula; dorsal scapular nerve (C5).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A frequent presenting feature of multiple sclerosis is:

options.D: Optic neuritis with painful loss of vision in one eye

questions.explanation: Also internuclear ophthalmoplegia.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Shumway-Cook & Woollacott, Motor Control; standard neurology texts (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: To determine the amino acid composition of a protein, it is first completely hydrolysed. Which method of hydrolysis tends to yield smaller peptides rather than fully free amino acids?
questions.explanation: While acid or alkali treatment can fully hydrolyse a protein down to free amino acids, treatment with enzymes typically results in smaller peptides rather than complete breakdown to individual amino acids, since most proteolytic enzymes have some bond specificity.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.sourceChapter: Proteins and Amino Acids — Determination of Primary Structure
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: A patent processus vaginalis that allows peritoneal fluid (but no bowel) to track down into the scrotum results in:
questions.explanation: When a patent processus vaginalis allows only peritoneal fluid (not bowel) to track into the scrotum, the result is a hydrocoele — typically a non-tender, transilluminating scrotal swelling, distinct from an inguinal hernia where bowel or other abdominal content is present.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: After repair of a peripheral nerve, a major objective of physiotherapy is to:

options.A: Maintain joint mobility, prevent contractures, and protect insensate skin while awaiting reinnervation

questions.explanation: Recovery is ~1 mm/day.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; Shumway-Cook & Woollacott, Motor Control; standard neurology texts (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The superior gluteal nerve supplies the:

options.D: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Injury leads to a Trendelenburg gait.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The hypothalamus regulates the body's internal environment (temperature, blood salt concentration, hormone levels) chiefly by controlling secretions from which gland?

options.C: The adrenal gland directly, bypassing the pituitary entirely

questions.explanation: The hypothalamus is connected to the pituitary gland and controls its hormone secretion into the bloodstream, either through nerve impulses or chemical releasing factors — linking the nervous system to the body's broader glandular (endocrine) system.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Forebrain: Hypothalamus and Pituitary
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: Duchenne muscular dystrophy is inherited as:
questions.explanation: Mutation in the dystrophin gene on Xp21; serum CK is markedly raised.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The initial priority of physiotherapy in an acute burn patient is:

options.A: Correct positioning and splinting to prevent contractures

questions.explanation: Plus chest care if inhalation injury is present.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The flexor withdrawal reflex is mediated by:

options.A: Polysynaptic pathways with reciprocal inhibition and crossed extensor reflex

questions.explanation: Painful stimulus: flexion of the stimulated limb, extension of the opposite limb.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: A side effect of long-term corticosteroid therapy relevant to physiotherapy is:
questions.explanation: Proximal muscle weakness; avoid heavy loading and be careful with fracture risk.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The right lymphatic duct drains lymph from:

options.B: The right upper quadrant of the body (right arm, right side of head and thorax)

questions.explanation: The thoracic duct drains the rest.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: On the International Death Certificate, the 'underlying cause of death' is recorded in Part I, and is defined as:

options.A: The immediate mode of dying, such as 'heart failure' or 'asthenia'
options.B: The disease or injury that initiated the chain of morbid events leading directly to death, or the circumstances of the accident/violence that produced the fatal injury
options.C: Any condition present at death regardless of its role in causing it
options.D: Only conditions diagnosed after an autopsy

questions.explanation: The underlying cause of death is the disease or injury that initiated the train of morbid events leading directly to death, or the circumstances of the accident/violence producing the fatal injury — the certificate explicitly notes this does NOT mean the immediate mode of dying (e.g. 'heart failure' or 'asthenia' are not acceptable as the underlying cause).
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Measurement of Mortality — International Death Certificate
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Cervical spondylotic myelopathy typically presents with:

options.B: Gait disturbance, hand clumsiness and upper motor neurone signs in the legs

questions.explanation: Hoffmann's sign and hyperreflexia indicate cord involvement.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Brukner & Khan, Clinical Sports Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Low-level laser therapy is believed to promote healing by:

options.A: Photochemical (photobiomodulation) effects such as increased ATP and cell proliferation

questions.explanation: Mitochondrial cytochrome c oxidase absorbs red/NIR light.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; Low & Reed, Electrotherapy Explained; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Which finding would usually contraindicate mobilising an ICU patient?

options.A: Unstable arrhythmias, active myocardial ischaemia or MAP < 60 mmHg

questions.explanation: Safety criteria include haemodynamic stability and acceptable oxygenation.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: After thoracotomy the physiotherapist should particularly teach:

options.A: Shoulder range-of-motion exercises on the operated side, deep breathing and supported coughing

questions.explanation: Prevents frozen shoulder and respiratory complications.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: For weight loss in obese individuals, the exercise recommendation is:

options.A: Gradually build up to 150–300 minutes a week of moderate aerobic activity plus resistance training
options.D: High-intensity impact exercise from the start

questions.explanation: Non-weight-bearing options such as swimming and cycling reduce joint load.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Aflatoxin B1 is associated with:
questions.explanation: Produced by Aspergillus flavus on stored grains; also hepatitis B.

questions.explanation: Pain on quadriceps contraction against patellar compression.
